test_title: PYST 17: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 15 Oct, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I have lived with my parents / in Mumbai / in a residential flat / yet two years.

options.text: I have lived with my parents

solution:
The erroneous part is: **yet two years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a **present perfect continuous tense**, which is used to show that something started in the past and has continued up until now.
 
• The correct phrase should be **"for two years"** instead of **"yet two years"**.
 
• Using "yet" in this context is incorrect; **"for"** is the appropriate preposition to indicate the duration of time.

Correct sentence: *I have lived with my parents in Mumbai in a residential flat **for** two years*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect Continuous Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + have/has + been + verb(+ing).
 
• **Example:** She has been working here for five years.
 
• **Usage: **Describes actions that started in the past and are still continuing or were happening recently.
 
 
 
• **Common Error:**
 
 
• Using incorrect prepositions for time duration. For example, **"since"** is used with specific **points in time**, and **"for"** is used with **periods of time**.
